entrypoints.summary: A crafted .tar or .tar.gz archive reaches controller-side extraction through features using the standard artifact manager, prominently Archive the artifacts and archiveArtifacts/archive Pipeline steps.
FilePath.readFromTar consumes tar entries and materializes them beneath the supplied extraction directory.

affected_components.role: Iterates tar entries, derives output paths, rejects escape and symlink conditions, and copies regular entry data.
Fixed-source symlink descendant boundary coverage; not established as a tar-extraction regression oracle.

code_slices.fixed: readFromTar normalizes the output path against the absolute base directory, rejects symlink ancestors and existing symlink targets, then copies regular tar-entry bytes only after those checks.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The same routine permits tar symbolic-link entries to be created, but guards subsequent regular-file output paths against symlink resolution.

negative_controls: Fixed versions reject entries whose path is outside the target directory.
Fixed versions reject extraction through symbolic links in the path or at the target location.
observability.positive_marker: A file is created at a location outside the selected extraction target; advisory examples identify a script in init.groovy.d or a plugin under JENKINS_HOME/plugins as controller code-execution routes.

preconditions: The vulnerable Jenkins version performs controller-side extraction of an attacker-controlled tar or tar.gz archive.
The attacker has Item/Configure permission or control of an agent process.
The Jenkins process has filesystem permission for the target location.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Tar archive with an entry path or target path that traverses a symbolic link outside the extraction root.
trigger_steps.summary: Provide a crafted tar or tar.gz archive whose entry/path uses symbolic-link resolution to target a location outside the extraction directory.

sources.concept: crafted tar archive extracted by Jenkins controller

impact.affected_asset: Jenkins controller filesystem, including JENKINS_HOME initialization-script and plugin directories.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause controller-side extraction of a crafted archive after obtaining Item/Configure permission or control over an agent process.
impact.security_effect: Arbitrary file creation/write with the filesystem permissions of the Jenkins process; controller-side placement of controller-consumed initialization scripts or plugins can result in code execution.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker with Item/Configure permission, or control of an agent process, supplies a crafted tar or gzip-compressed tar archive to a Jenkins feature that extracts it on the controller.
Archive extraction did not safely handle symbolic links, allowing an archive entry's destination to resolve outside the intended target directory.

The extraction implementation creates the entry output path and copies non-symlink entry bytes to it; the fixed code now rejects normalized paths outside the base directory, symlink ancestors, and an existing symlink at the output path before that copy.

A crafted archive can write files to arbitrary filesystem locations permitted to the Jenkins process; controller extraction can place scripts in JENKINS_HOME/init.groovy.d or plugins in JENKINS_HOME/plugins, which the advisory identifies as routes to code execution.

failure.operation: Filesystem file creation/write while extracting a non-symlink tar entry through a symlink-resolved path

primary_invariant.kind: archive extraction path containment and symlink non-traversal
primary_invariant.statement: Every materialized tar entry must remain beneath the extraction target and extraction must not write through symbolic links in an ancestor path or at the target location.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Prior behavior did not safely handle symbolic links during tar and tar.gz extraction, so a crafted entry could resolve to an arbitrary filesystem location outside the target directory.

raw_refs.role: official finding advisory and version scope

quality.review_notes: The vendor advisory establishes trigger conditions, version scope, controller-side impact path, and fixed behavior. Fixed FilePath code directly shows normalized base-directory checks and symlink-path/target rejection before file copying. The supplied FilePathTest excerpt covers isDescendant symlink behavior, not a dedicated crafted-tar rejection test, and no vulnerable-version run result or public reproducer is present; therefore no executable harness is asserted.

remediation.invariant_restored: Refuse tar and tar.gz entries whose normalized output path escapes the target directory and prevent writes where any path ancestor or the target location is a symbolic link.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The attacker controls archive contents and must be able to cause controller-side artifact extraction through Item/Configure permission or control of an agent process.
data_structure_invariants: Normalized absolute output path starts with the normalized absolute extraction base directory.
No ancestor from the output parent up to the extraction base directory is a symbolic link.
A regular-file entry does not overwrite through an existing symbolic link.
state_context.state_machine: Archive entry iteration: obtain entry name; validate containment; inspect output-parent ancestry for symlinks; create directory or symbolic link entry, or reject an existing output symlink before copying a regular entry.
